Monaragala District Profile

Official Geographical & Statistical Data from Wikipedia

District Overview

Introduction

Monaragala is a district in the Uva Province of Sri Lanka. It is the second-largest district among the 25 districts of Sri Lanka, spanning an extensive land area. The district is known for its rich tapestry of dense forest covers, sprawling rubber and sugar cane plantations, and deep historical resonance linked with ancient Sri Lankan kingdoms.

Quick Statistical Profile (Uva Province)
Country Sri Lanka
Province Uva Province
Capital Monaragala Town
Total Area 5,639 km² (Second largest in Sri Lanka)
Major Crops Paddy, Sugar Cane, Rubber, Vegetables

Geography & Climate

Terrain and Weather

Geographically, Monaragala predominantly falls within the dry zone of Sri Lanka, though it features transitional topography heading towards the central highlands. The southern and eastern sectors are mostly flat plains, while the western parts roll into mountainous terrain. The district experiences significant rainfall during the North-East monsoon season, keeping its diverse dry-mixed evergreen forests thriving.

Administrative Divisions

Divisional Secretariats

The Monaragala district is divided into 11 Divisional Secretariat (DS) Divisions for decentralized governance and administrative smoothness. The major key towns and secretariats include:


  • Monaragala Town & Wellawaya
  • Kataragama & Buttala
  • Bibile & Medagama
  • Siyambalanduwa, Badalkumbura, & Thanamalwila
  • Madulla & Sevanagala

Archaeological & Historical Sites

Kataragama Holy City

A multi-religious sacred city located on the banks of the Menik Ganga, historically connected to the Ruhunu Kingdom. It attracts thousands of Buddhist, Hindu, and indigenous Vedda pilgrims annually.

Maligawila Archaeological Site

Renowned for housing the massive 7th-century freestanding Buddha statue, sculpted skillfully out of a single crystalline limestone block, along with the Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva statue.

Gal Oya National Park Image

Gal Oya National Park

Home to the Senanayake Samudraya, Sri Lanka's largest reservoir, this park is famous for its boat safaris and herds of wild elephants swimming between islands in search of food.

Buduruwagala Image

Buduruwagala Rock Temple

A cluster of seven colossal Buddha and Bodhisattva statues carved directly into a rock face near Wellawaya, dating to the 9th-10th century, with traces of the original stucco and paint still visible.

Sella Kataragama Image

Sella Kataragama

Believed to be the original site of the Kataragama shrine before it moved to its present location, this quiet forest hermitage retains a serene and ancient spiritual atmosphere.

Yudaganawa Stupa

One of the largest ancient stupas in Sri Lanka, dating back to the 2nd century BC. Historically documented as the battlefield where Prince Dutugemunu and his brother Prince Tissa clashed.
